capabilities: define highlighters from search terms or JavaScript regular expressions
render placeholders such as =TODO= as badges showing the first capture group
highlight all occurrences of the word under the cursor or selected text
apply highlights in reading view and PDF export
import highlighter configurations from the Dynamic Highlights plugin as JSON
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later. Regex lookbehind does not work on iOS older than 16.4. Import from Dynamic Highlights keeps that plugin installed during migration and saves its custom CSS as a separate snippet.
intentEvidence: Inspired by Dynamic Highlights by NothingIsLost, which is no longer listed in the community plugins directory.
problem: Obsidian only highlights text you mark manually; it cannot automatically style every match of a term or pattern across the editor, reading view and exports.

relations.evidence: Inspired by Dynamic Highlights by NothingIsLost, which is no longer listed

summary: Rule-based text highlighter that styles matches of search terms and regular expressions as backgrounds, badges, underlines or colors.
